method: official web sources only, read by an automated assistant; not a human site visit

entries.name: Battery Point Lighthouse
entries.address: 235 Lighthouse Way (foot of Lighthouse Way), Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: An 1856 lighthouse on a small tidal island at the end of Lighthouse Way, run by the Del Norte County Historical Society and still used as a private aid to navigation. Tours take visitors through the keepers' quarters and up into the light tower, but the island can only be reached on foot at low tide across about 200 feet of rock and beach, so visits depend on the tide table.
entries.cost_note: Admission charged (members admitted free) but no price is published on the Society's pages.
entries.access_notes: Tours include a climb into the light tower; crossing to the island is over rocks and beach. No accessibility statement on the official page.
entries.hours_note: 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., tide permitting, in both the April-September and October-March seasons per the Society page; tour times follow the tide log and 'are not always accurate'. Call ahead.
entries.notes: Official page warns of sneaker waves near the rocks and shore. City parks page lists the address as 235 Lighthouse Way.

entries.name: Del Norte County Historical Society Main Museum
entries.address: 577 H Street, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: The Historical Society's main museum in downtown Crescent City at 6th and H Streets holds local history collections, with linked topic pages on the Tolowa and Yurok peoples, regional lighthouses and the 1964 tsunami. It has a gift shop and is paired with the Battery Point Lighthouse under one membership.
entries.cost_note: Admission charged (members free); no price listed on the official pages fetched.
entries.hours_note: Hours not listed on the pages fetched; call to confirm.
entries.notes: Society search snippet notes cameras/photographs are not allowed inside the museum.

entries.name: Ocean World
entries.address: 304 Highway 101 South, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: A small private aquarium on US 101 at the south end of town offering a guided tour of roughly 45 minutes that includes a touch tide pool, a shark and bat-ray tank, resident seals and sea lions, and a sea-lion show. Tours leave about every 20 minutes and are first come, first served.
entries.cost_note: Ages 12 and over $16.95; ages 3-11 $10.95; 2 and under free (as listed on the official site).
entries.access_notes: No accessibility statement on the official site; call to ask.
entries.hours_note: Open daily; gift shop 9:00 am-6:00 pm, tours 9:15 am-4:30 pm, last tour varies with natural light; call ahead for late-day tours.

entries.name: Beachfront Park and Kid's Town (KidTown) playground
entries.address: Play Street / Front Street at Crescent City Harbor, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: The city's main waterfront park along the harbor, hosting community events and bundling several family draws: the Kid's Town playground on Play Street with swings, a wheelchair swing, tot lot, picnic areas and restrooms, plus a fenced dog park, a 23-hole disc golf course, soccer fields, BBQ pits and a stretch of the California Coastal Trail with ADA beach access at Howe Park. The municipal pool and the Northcoast Marine Mammal Center sit on the same grounds.
entries.cost_note: Public city park; no fee stated on the official page.
entries.access_notes: City page lists a 'Wheelchair swing' at Kid's Town and 'ADA beach access' at Howe Park on the Coastal Trail. No statement about restroom or path accessibility.
entries.hours_note: Hours not listed on the official page.
entries.geo_source: Google Maps link for Kid's Town on https://www.crescentcity.org/BeachfrontPark-1
entries.notes: A March 2025 city environmental study describes a planned new accessible, inclusive play area next to Kid's Town; completion status not confirmed.

entries.name: Fred Endert Municipal Pool
entries.address: 1001 Play St., Crescent City, CA 95531 (city parks page lists 1000 Play Street)
entries.summary: Crescent City's indoor municipal pool in Beachfront Park, with a 25-yard pool, a waterslide, a hot tub and a sauna. It runs swim lessons from 6 months up, youth programs and open/lap swim, and the Del Norte Healthcare District sponsors a free all-ages recreation swim on Saturdays.
entries.cost_note: Daily rates: youth (7-17) $4, adult (18-63) $6, senior (64+) $5; passes and memberships available; free Saturday recreation swim.
entries.access_notes: Pool history on the official site says the renovated facility reopened as a 'new ADA-friendly facility'. No detail on lifts or ramps.
entries.hours_note: Posted schedule (Sept 1-Dec 31, 2026): Mon-Fri 5:30 am-8:10 pm, Sat 6:00 am-7 pm, Sun closed. Check the weekly schedule for program times.
entries.geo_source: Google Maps link for Fred Endert Pool on https://www.crescentcity.org/BeachfrontPark-1
entries.notes: Rules: children 10 and under must pass a swim test to be in the pool without an adult; lap swim open to ages 3+ who can swim 25 yards continuously; riding the slide with a child is not permitted. crescentcity.org/directory/SwimmingPool redirects to crescentcitypool.com.

entries.name: B Street Pier
entries.address: 301 B St South, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: A large wooden public viewing pier reaching out over Crescent City bay from the west end of the waterfront, with panoramic views of the harbor and lighthouse. The city lists crabbing and sea-lion watching as the main draws, and the pier can be rented for special events.
entries.cost_note: Public city facility; no fee stated.
entries.notes: This is the official place to see harbor sea lions; the Harbor District site has no dedicated sea-lion viewing page.

entries.name: Fraser Park playground
entries.address: Corner of 9th and Taylor Streets, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: A 1.35-acre neighborhood park near the ocean with an updated community playground, swings, a basketball court, open lawn and restrooms. It sits next to Brother Jonathan Park, sharing its lawns and restrooms, and is listed as dog friendly.
entries.cost_note: Public city park; no fee stated.

entries.name: Peterson Park skate park and sports fields
entries.address: 5th and F Streets, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: A 7.4-acre city park whose amenities include a county-run skate park, a baseball/softball field, tennis courts and a community garden. It is the only skate park named on an official local-government page.
entries.cost_note: Public park; no fee stated.
entries.notes: Official mention of the skate park is a single line ('County Ran Skate Park'); no rules, hours or helmet policy published.

entries.name: Brother Jonathan Park and Overlook
entries.address: 9th Street and Pebble Beach Drive, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: A 1.36-acre waterfront park beside Fraser Park with lawns, benches, a memorial and gravesite for the 1865 Brother Jonathan shipwreck, and an observation point across Pebble Beach Drive. The overlook has parking and benches and looks south to Battery Point Lighthouse and north to Preston Island.
entries.cost_note: Public city park; no fee stated.
entries.notes: Closest official page for the Pebble Beach Drive shoreline; 'Pebble Beach' itself has no official page.

entries.name: Pyke Field playground and softball fields
entries.address: 1005 H Street, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: A Del Norte County recreation site at the county Recreation Department address on H Street, listed as a playground together with softball fields. The county map page gives little more than the name and location.
entries.cost_note: Public county facility; no fee stated.

entries.name: Northcoast Marine Mammal Center
entries.address: 424 Howe Dr., Crescent City, CA 95531 (in Beachfront Park)
entries.summary: A nonprofit seal and sea lion rescue and rehabilitation center in Beachfront Park near the lighthouse, with outdoor animal pens, a harbor seal pup room and a gift shop/information center. Its stated aim includes public education about marine mammals, and it runs on donations and memberships.
entries.cost_note: No admission fee listed; donations requested.
entries.hours_note: Only gift-shop winter hours are posted: Thu 1-4, Fri-Sat 11-4. Whether animal areas are open to viewing is not stated; call first.
entries.notes: Rescue hotline (707) 951-4722 is for stranded animals, not visitor questions.

entries.name: Crescent City Information Center (Redwood National and State Parks headquarters bookstore)
entries.address: 1111 Second Street, Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: The park headquarters information center and bookstore in downtown Crescent City, one of five visitor centers for Redwood National and State Parks. Staff provide orientation and trip planning, and the 2026 park guide says every center hands out maps, Junior Ranger books and passport stamps; park wifi is available here.
entries.cost_note: No entrance fee for Redwood National Park.
entries.access_notes: NPS accessibility page says visitor centers generally offer accessible options and tactile models, but gives no site-specific statement.
entries.hours_note: Current hours not published on the fetched NPS pages ('seasonal schedules'); call 707-464-6101.
entries.notes: 2026 visitor guide labels it 'Crescent City Bookstore / Park Headquarters, 2nd and K Streets'.

entries.name: Hiouchi Visitor Center
entries.address: Highway 199, 9 miles east/northeast of Crescent City, CA 95531
entries.summary: The NPS visitor center on US 199 at Hiouchi, the main stop for information on scenic drives, trails and camping in the northern (Jedediah Smith) part of the parks. Like the other centers it offers maps, Junior Ranger books and passport stamps, and it hosts ranger porch programs.
entries.access_notes: Park-wide statement only: visitor centers offer accessible options and tactile models.
entries.hours_note: Current hours not published on the fetched NPS pages; call 707-464-6101.

entries.name: Jedediah Smith Visitor Center (seasonal)
entries.address: Inside Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park near the Smith River, off US 199, 9 miles northeast of Crescent City
entries.summary: A summer-season visitor center and campground store inside the state park campground by the Smith River. It provides the same orientation, maps and Junior Ranger materials as the other park centers during the months it is open.
entries.cost_note: The surrounding campground/day-use area charges an $8 per-vehicle day-use fee.
entries.hours_note: NPS directions page: open during the summer months only.

entries.name: Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park - campground day-use area and river beach
entries.address: Jedediah Smith campground entrance road off US 199, 9 miles east of Crescent City (west of Hiouchi)
entries.summary: The developed heart of Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park, where a paved day-use area beside the Smith River gives access to a gravel river beach, a small-boat launch, picnic tables, drinking water, vault toilets and the trailheads for the Nature River Trail and the summer footbridge to Stout Grove. The state park page lists picnicking, fishing, interpretive exhibits and geocaching; the river beach is popular for swimming but has no lifeguard.
entries.cost_note: $8 per vehicle day-use fee (cash on site); special rates may apply at peak times; federal and state park passes accepted.
entries.access_notes: State Parks accessibility page: accessible picnic area at the Nature River trailhead, accessible parking and restrooms near both Nature River trailheads, 10 accessible picnic tables in the picnic area, accessible campsites and cabins.
entries.hours_note: Day use sunrise to sunset; campground open all year.
entries.geo_source: Google Maps directions link on https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=413
entries.notes: Dogs not allowed on trails. Seasonal Stout Grove footbridge listed as removed on the NPS conditions page as of 2026-10-14 (normally installed late June to late September).

entries.name: Crescent Beach Day Use Area
entries.address: Enderts Beach Road off US 101, about 2.5 miles south of Crescent City
entries.summary: A long sandy beach just south of town in Redwood National Park, reached by a short paved road with plenty of car and RV parking, picnic tables, a fire pit and a vault toilet. It is a place for beachcombing and play rather than swimming, since the water is cold with swift currents; elk are often seen along the road.
entries.cost_note: No fee listed; Redwood National Park has no entrance fee.
entries.access_notes: NPS lists 'Wheelchair Accessible' among amenities and says beach wheelchairs can be reserved.
entries.notes: Leashed pets allowed; vehicles not allowed on the beach. Starting point of the flat Coastal Trail Crescent Beach section.

entries.name: Crescent Beach Overlook
entries.address: Near the end of Enderts Beach Road, 3 miles south of Crescent City
entries.summary: A bluff-top viewpoint at the top of Enderts Beach Road looking back over Crescent Beach and the city, with interpretive signs, three picnic tables and a scenic viewpoint used for whale watching. Parking at the overlook itself holds only two vehicles; more parking and an accessible vault toilet are a few hundred feet away at the road end.
entries.access_notes: NPS notes an accessible vault toilet at the Enderts Beach Road parking area; nothing stated about the overlook platform.
entries.notes: Motorhomes, RVs and trailers not advised beyond the Crescent Beach picnic area.

entries.name: Tolowa Dunes State Park
entries.address: Kellogg Road / Lower Lake Road area, about 2 miles north of Crescent City (park office: 1111 Second Street, Crescent City, CA 95531)
entries.summary: A large coastal park of dunes, wetlands, forest and ocean beach between Crescent City and the Smith River mouth, with many miles of hiking, biking and horse trails and a long undeveloped beach. From US 101 take Northcrest Drive north (it becomes Lake Earl Drive), turn left on Lower Lake Road and go west on Kellogg Road to reach the beach area.
entries.cost_note: No day-use fee listed on the official page; California State Library Parks Pass accepted.
entries.access_notes: Page links to accessibility info but states nothing specific.
entries.hours_note: Open year-round, day use sunrise to sunset. Campground closed until further notice.
entries.geo_source: Google Maps directions link on https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=430
entries.notes: Dogs not allowed. No park brochure available; coastal access points reported as poorly signed in state publications. Castle Rock / Southwest Seal Rock special closures apply offshore.

entries.name: Lake Earl Wildlife Area
entries.address: 1180 Lakeview Drive, Crescent City, CA 95531 (information center 1.4 miles along Old Mill Road)
entries.summary: A roughly 6,100-acre state wildlife area around Lake Earl and Lake Tolowa, the largest coastal lagoon on the West Coast, managed by CDFW for birdwatching, hiking, fishing, non-motorized boating and seasonal waterfowl hunting. There is an information kiosk, restrooms and parking, and two boat launches at the ends of Lakeview Drive and Buzzini Road.
entries.cost_note: No pass required for entry; fishing licence needed to fish and not sold on site.
entries.access_notes: Official page states 'There are no accessibility improvements on this property.'
entries.hours_note: Not listed. Hunting seasons and dune-restoration closures apply on some days in fall/winter; check the Emergency Closures page.
entries.notes: No dogs unless hunting; no camping; drones need a permit. Families should note active waterfowl hunting in season.

entries.name: Pelican State Beach
entries.address: US Highway 101 N at Gilbert Way, Smith River, CA (21 miles north of Crescent City)
entries.summary: California's northernmost beach, a small undeveloped and secluded state beach right at the Oregon border with parking, beach access and surf-watching. There are no facilities, and the page recommends layered clothing for changeable weather.
entries.cost_note: No fee listed on the official page.
entries.geo_source: Google Maps directions link on https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=412
entries.notes: Dogs not allowed on the beach except service animals. About 30 minutes' drive from Crescent City.

entries.name: Clifford Kamph Memorial Park
entries.address: West side of US 101, about 2 miles south of the Oregon border and 4.8 miles north of Smith River (Parks office: 840 9th Street, Suite 11, Crescent City)
entries.summary: A small county park of just over 3 acres on a bluff above the Pacific near the state line, with 14 tent-only campsites and a beach below. It was dedicated in 1949 in memory of a WWII pilot and is one of three Del Norte County campgrounds.
entries.cost_note: No day-use fee listed; camping $20 per night (includes 2 vehicles), $5 each extra vehicle.
entries.notes: Pets welcome on leash. Campsites first come, first served.

entries.name: Florence Keller Regional Park
entries.address: Off Elk Valley Crossroad, 3 miles north of Crescent City on US 101 (county lists 3400 Cunningham Lane; Parks office 840 9th Street, Suite 11)
entries.summary: A county park in second-growth redwoods just north of town with 50 campsites, seven short easy-walking trails (one wheelchair accessible), and two rentable picnic areas; the large picnic area has a playground, swings, horseshoe pits, a volleyball court and tetherball. It is the closest redwood-shaded park with a playground to Crescent City.
entries.cost_note: No general day-use fee listed; picnic areas rent for $60 (small) and $120 (large) per day by reservation; camping $20 per night.
entries.access_notes: County page: seven trails, 'one of which is wheelchair accessible'. No statement about restrooms or playground surface.

trail.family_note: Seven 'easy-walking' trails per the county page; lengths not given.

entries.notes: Pets welcome on leash. County pages give two different addresses (3400 Cunningham Lane and the parks office).

entries.name: Ruby Van Deventer County Park
entries.address: Highway 197 (North Bank Road), between US 101 and US 199 (Parks office: 840 9th Street, Suite 11, Crescent City)
entries.summary: A 54-acre county park stretching a quarter mile along the Smith River on North Bank Road, with 18 campsites, a group picnic area and river access about 50 yards from the sites. The county lists swimming, kayaking and seasonal fishing as the main activities.
entries.cost_note: No day-use fee listed; group picnic area $45 per day by reservation; camping $20 per night.
entries.notes: Pets on leash. Unguarded river swimming.

entries.name: Forks River Access and Boat Ramp (Smith River NRA)
entries.address: Milepost 0.25 on South Fork Road, 1/4 mile south of the junction with US 199, east of Hiouchi
entries.summary: A Forest Service day-use site at the confluence area of the Smith River forks with an asphalt parking lot, boat ramp and vault toilets, used for swimming, sunbathing, non-motorized boating and fishing. It is the nearest Smith River NRA river access to Crescent City.
entries.cost_note: 'No pass required.'
entries.hours_note: Day use only; no overnight camping.
entries.notes: No potable water. Unguarded river swimming.

entries.name: Panther Flat Picnic Area and swimming holes (Smith River NRA)
entries.address: US 199, 2.5 miles east of the Gasquet visitor center
entries.summary: A no-fee day-use picnic area next to the Panther Flat campground on the Middle Fork Smith River, with eight picnic tables, grills, water and a horseshoe pit. Two short paths lead from the picnic area to river swimming holes, one with a small sandy beach.
entries.cost_note: Picnic area is 'no-fee, day-use only'; campground charges separately.
entries.access_notes: Page says 'Accessible sites available' and notes accessible flush toilets for the campground; not stated for the picnic area.
entries.notes: About 35-40 minutes from Crescent City; at the edge of the 30-minute radius. Fire restrictions in effect.

entries.name: Smith River National Recreation Area Visitor Center (Gasquet Ranger Station)
entries.address: 10600 Highway 199, Gasquet, CA 95543
entries.summary: The Forest Service office and visitor center for the Smith River National Recreation Area on US 199 in Gasquet, offering information services, free maps and brochures, souvenirs and campfire permits. It is the place to ask about river access, swimming holes and trail conditions along the undammed Smith River.
entries.hours_note: Summer hours (listed as currently in effect): 8 am-4:30 pm seven days a week; standard hours 8-4:30 Mon-Fri, closed federal holidays. Call to confirm.

entries.name: Trees of Mystery
entries.address: 15500 US-101, Klamath, CA 95548
entries.summary: A family-owned roadside redwood attraction marked by giant Paul Bunyan and Babe statues, where one ticket covers the forest trails, the Redwood Canopy Trail of suspended bridges, the End of the Trail Native American museum and the SkyTrail gondola, an 8-10 minute ride in enclosed six-passenger cars to a ridge-top ocean view deck. The site suggests allowing at least half a day.
entries.cost_note: General (13-59) $30; seniors $25; kids 3-12 $15; 0-2 free. Everything included with admission.
entries.access_notes: FAQ: 'up in our trails we are not Wheel Chair accessible'; a shuttle to SkyTrail is offered for those who cannot easily walk the trail, and the gondola cars are described as handicapped accessible.
entries.hours_note: Trail entrance 9:00 am-4:00 pm, museum 9-5, gift shop 9-5:30; open every day except Thanksgiving and Christmas, half day Christmas Eve. Call for changes.
entries.notes: Leashed pets welcome everywhere except the Redwood Canopy Trail. Wilderness Trail descent is for experienced hikers only. Roughly 30-35 minutes south of Crescent City.

entries.name: Klamath River Overlook
entries.address: End of Requa Road, about 2.25 miles from the signed US 101 exit, 18.5 miles south of Crescent City
entries.summary: A viewpoint 650 feet above the Pacific where the Klamath River meets the ocean, reached by a steep, narrow paved road through the historic village of Requa. NPS describes it as a top spot for whale watching, seabirds and coastal views, and it is the southern trailhead of the Coastal Trail's Klamath section.
entries.access_notes: The Coastal Trail: Klamath page lists an accessible restroom among its amenities but does not say where it is.
entries.notes: Motorhomes, RVs and trailers not recommended on Requa Road.

entries.name: Lagoon Creek Day Use Area
entries.address: Signed turnoff on US 101, halfway between Crescent City and Klamath
entries.summary: A roadside picnic area beside a freshwater pond right off US 101, with picnic tables, flush and accessible restrooms, interpretive exhibits and car and RV parking. Herons feed in the pond, and the easy Yurok Loop Trail starts on the ocean side of the lot, with Coastal Trail access south to the Klamath River Overlook.
entries.access_notes: NPS amenities list includes 'Wheelchair Accessible' and 'Restroom - Accessible'. The Yurok Loop Trail itself is unpaved.
entries.notes: Starting point for a quarter-mile walk on the Coastal Trail to the False Klamath Cove tidepools.

entries.name: False Klamath Cove beach (Wilson Beach)
entries.address: Southbound-only pullout on the ocean side of US 101, halfway between Crescent City and Klamath
entries.summary: A rugged cobbled beach in Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park beside the highway, where families can walk the shore and, when conditions allow, explore tidepools at the north end near Wilson Creek. The state park page describes it as a half-mile sandy strolling and tidepooling beach that is not safe for swimming.
entries.notes: NPS warns southbound drivers to take great care entering and leaving the pullout; no northbound access. State park page: steep slope, rough seas and cold water make it unsafe for swimming.

entries.name: Howland Hill Road scenic drive
entries.address: From US 101 1 mile south of Crescent City, east on Elk Valley Road 1 mile, then right on Howland Hill Road; ends at South Fork Road / US 199 near Hiouchi
entries.summary: A 10-mile, roughly 45-minute one-way drive on a narrow, winding and mostly gravel road through old-growth redwoods in Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park, with pull-outs and the trailheads for Boy Scout Tree, Grove of Titans and Stout Grove. Motorhomes, RVs and trailers will not fit.
entries.cost_note: Driving park roads is free.
entries.hours_note: Listed as open on the NPS conditions page as of 2026-10-14; road is sometimes closed, check conditions.
entries.notes: Unpaved after about 1.5 miles; dusty in summer; parking very limited at trailheads in summer.

entries.name: Stout Memorial Grove Trail
entries.address: Paved access road at the east end of Howland Hill Road, Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park; summer-only alternative from the campground day-use area via seasonal footbridge
entries.summary: A half-mile loop through one of the most photographed old-growth groves on the Smith River floodplain, flat and easy once past the initial descent from the parking lot, with a spur down to the river. Reaching it means driving the unpaved east end of Howland Hill Road, or in summer walking about 1.3 miles from the campground day-use area and crossing the seasonal footbridge.
entries.cost_note: Free from Howland Hill Road; $8 day-use fee if parking at the campground day-use area.
entries.access_notes: NPS: 'This is not an ADA accessible trail' (4-6 ft wood and aggregate tread, switchbacks). State Parks accessibility page calls the loop 'generally accessible' apart from steep sections and a 500-ft steep service-road descent, with accessible restroom and parking at the lot.
entries.hours_note: Day, dawn and dusk; year round from Howland Hill Road.

trail.surface: Wood and aggregate, 4-6 feet wide, switchbacks to the river
trail.family_note: 'After the initial descent from the parking lot, the trail is easy and flat' (NPS). Allow 1-2 hours including travel.
trail.warnings: No RV or trailer parking; Howland Hill Road not suitable for large vehicles. Seasonal footbridges normally late June-late September and listed as removed on 2026-10-14. Pets not allowed. Vault toilet at trailhead.

entries.name: Simpson-Reed Trail
entries.address: Walker Road, 0.1 mile north of US 199 (sharp, easy-to-miss turn between Crescent City and Hiouchi), Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park
entries.summary: The easiest old-growth walk in the north of the parks: a level 0.8-mile loop on a wide compacted gravel path past huge redwoods, nurse logs, ferns and a creek, with interpretive panels. The connecting Peterson Memorial loop adds about half a mile.
entries.access_notes: NPS: 'ADA accessible trail made of aggregate gravel that is four to five feet wide'; accessible parking and a non-flush accessible restroom off Walker Road; State Parks lists grades generally under 5%.

trail.warnings: Limited parking; no RV or trailer parking. Pets not allowed.

entries.notes: Listed as open with no restrictions on the NPS conditions page, 2026-10-14.

entries.name: Grove of Titans Trail
entries.address: Marked trailhead on the east side of the eastern half of Howland Hill Road, Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park; best reached from US 199 near Hiouchi
entries.summary: A 1.5-mile loop (the 2026 guide lists 1.7 miles out and back) to a cluster of the largest known coast redwoods, where about 1,500 feet of elevated metal boardwalk completed in 2022 protects the forest floor and lets visitors walk among the giants. The route is compacted gravel and duff with roots and many metal steps.
entries.access_notes: NPS: 'not ADA accessible'; boardwalk has many metal steps.

trail.surface: Compacted gravel, dirt and duff about 4 ft wide, plus 1,500 ft of elevated metal boardwalk with steps
trail.family_note: Non-level with some grades and metal stairs; 1-2 hours.
trail.warnings: No RVs or vehicles towing trailers on Howland Hill Road; parking very limited in summer. Pets not allowed. Vault toilet at trailhead.

entries.name: Boy Scout Tree Trail
entries.address: Marked trailhead and parking on the north side of Howland Hill Road, about 3.5 miles east of Elk Valley Road
entries.summary: A moderate 2.8-mile one-way (5.5 miles round trip) walk through old-growth redwoods to Fern Falls, with an unmarked spur at about 2.5 miles to the double-trunked Boy Scout Tree. NPS suggests a half day and about 900 feet of elevation change, so it suits older children used to hiking rather than toddlers.
entries.access_notes: 2026 park guide hike table marks 'Accessible? No'.
entries.hours_note: Partially open since Aug 4, 2026: a fallen tree blocks the trail 1.75 miles in and is difficult to climb over (NPS conditions page, 2026-10-14).

trail.surface: Dirt trail with steep grades and switchbacks
trail.family_note: Moderate; 3-4 hours; allow at least half a day.
trail.warnings: Many vehicle break-ins at this trailhead. Howland Hill Road unsuitable for trailers and motorhomes; parking limited; dusty in summer. No climbing on or near waterfalls. Cell coverage unreliable. Pets not allowed. Vault toilet at trailhead.

entries.notes: Included as the longest 'family-suitable' option; best for school-age children.

entries.name: Nature River Trail (Jedediah Smith day-use area)
entries.address: Trailheads in the Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park day-use area and campground, off US 199
entries.summary: A 0.6-mile accessible trail on compacted aggregate linking the day-use area and the campground through redwood forest with views of the Smith River. An accessible picnic area sits at the day-use trailhead, with accessible parking and restrooms near both ends.
entries.cost_note: $8 per vehicle day-use fee at the campground entrance station.
entries.access_notes: State Parks: 0.6-mile accessible trail, compacted aggregate, generally flat; one armored crossing may be challenging in rain; accessible parking, restrooms and picnic area.
entries.geo_source: Google Maps directions link on https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=413 (park entrance)

trail.family_note: Stated accessible and generally flat; stroller-suitable by surface description (not stated by the park).
trail.warnings: Armored crossing can be difficult during rain. Dogs not allowed on trails.

entries.name: Enderts Beach via Coastal Trail (Last Chance section, north end)
entries.address: Trailhead at the end of Enderts Beach Road, 3 miles south of Crescent City off US 101
entries.summary: A short, moderately steep walk of about 0.5-0.6 mile down the first stretch of the Last Chance section of the Coastal Trail to a sheltered beach with some of the most accessible tidepools near Crescent City. Low tide is needed for tidepooling; the trailhead bulletin board and visitor center post tide times.
entries.access_notes: Accessible vault toilet at the Enderts Beach Road parking area; trail itself has steep grades.

trail.surface: Dirt trail with some steep grades
trail.family_note: Moderate per NPS; tidepools at the end. 2026 guide lists it as a 0.5 mi / 0.8 km hike.
trail.warnings: Check low tide times before going. Last Chance section is often affected by landslides; check conditions. Limited RV/trailer parking; RVs not advised beyond the Crescent Beach picnic area. No bikes on the beach.

entries.name: Coastal Trail - Crescent Beach section
entries.address: Starts at the Crescent Beach picnic area on Enderts Beach Road off US 101, south of Crescent City
entries.summary: A flat, meandering 3.5-mile section of the California Coastal Trail along the back of Crescent Beach that NPS itself calls kid-friendly. Walk as far as you like and turn around, with elk often grazing in the meadows beside the trail.
entries.access_notes: No accessibility statement for the trail; the Crescent Beach day-use area at the start is listed as wheelchair accessible.

trail.warnings: Elk are wild and can get defensive if threatened; keep distance.

entries.name: Yurok Loop Trail
entries.address: Trailhead on the ocean (west) side of the Lagoon Creek day-use parking lot, signed turnoff on US 101 halfway between Crescent City and Klamath
entries.summary: An easy one-mile coastal loop (1.25 miles in the 2026 guide) from the Lagoon Creek picnic area through coastal forest and wildflowers to bluff views of sea stacks and seabirds, about ten minutes' walk from the car to the first viewpoint. The first half mile doubles as the Coastal Trail, which continues 4 miles south to the Klamath River Overlook.
entries.access_notes: 2026 park guide hike table marks 'Accessible? No'; trail is unpaved. Accessible restrooms at the Lagoon Creek lot.

trail.family_note: NPS: 'an easy trail' suitable for children; non-level with some grades, not steep; about 100 ft elevation; 45 min-1.25 hrs.
trail.warnings: Pets not allowed on park trails. Excellent parking for RVs and trailers.

entries.notes: Bring binoculars for seabirds.

entries.name: Mill Creek Campground Trail (Del Norte Coast Redwoods SP)
entries.address: Adjacent to the Mill Creek Campground entrance road, off US 101 about 7 miles south of Crescent City (campground 2 miles east of the highway)
entries.summary: A 0.7-mile easy, flat trail along the Mill Creek Campground road in Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park that NPS lists as suitable for children, connecting to the 1-mile Alder Basin Trail and the campground's Nature Loop. The campground is seasonal and a gate blocks vehicle access off-season, when visitors park along US 101.
entries.cost_note: State park vehicle day-use fee of $8 is charged at the developed campground entrance station when open; off-season access on foot from US 101.
entries.hours_note: Mill Creek Day Use Area partially closed on weekdays; open to the public on weekends for day use with the gate locked each evening (NPS conditions page, 2026-10-14).
entries.geo_source: Google Maps directions link on https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=414 (park/campground)

trail.warnings: Seasonal gate on Mill Creek Campground Road; weekday closures in effect. Dogs not allowed on trails. Nearby Damnation Creek trailhead closed by Caltrans until further notice.

entries.notes: Nature Loop Trail (1 mi, 'easy 20-minute stroll' with some steep grades) starts across from the entrance station.

entries.name: Darlingtonia Trail (Smith River NRA)
entries.address: US 199 east of Gasquet, about 1 mile east of Panther Flat Campground (per Forest Service pages); managed from 10600 Highway 199, Gasquet
entries.summary: A very short graveled loop to a bog full of carnivorous California pitcher plants, with two wooden viewing platforms, designed for wheelchair access. It is a quick, unusual nature stop for children on the way up US 199.
entries.cost_note: No fee information on the page.
entries.access_notes: Forest Service: 'A graveled path and two wooden viewing platforms provide good wheelchair access to this unique site.'

trail.surface: Graveled path with wooden viewing platforms
trail.family_note: 'Short walk' per Forest Service; length not stated.
trail.warnings: Location given only relative to Panther Flat Campground; confirm at the Gasquet visitor center. Fire restrictions in effect. About 35-40 minutes from Crescent City.
